sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- write: Create or overwrite files
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

content.text: Generate an animated SVG of an anteater riding a unicycle while juggling bottles.

content.thinking:
I'm settling on an animated SVG, so I'll write it out as a file. The plan is an 800x600 scene with a ground line, an anteater on a unicycle, a spinning wheel and pedals, and bottles juggled along arcs, all driven by SMIL and CSS animations. I'm starting with the sky gradient and ground.

Still working out the SVG's unicycle and anteater details, including how the legs should follow the pedals.

Still working out the knee positions for the anteater's legs, since the thigh and shin each need to be long enough to reach the pedals at every point in the crank's turn.

Still computing the knee joints for the anteater's legs, working out each pedal position and the bend direction for the thigh and shin.

Still computing the knee joints for each pedal position, checking the bend direction and leg lengths as the crank turns.

Still computing the knee joints for the leg positions at the remaining pedal angles, checking the bend direction and leg lengths.

Still computing the knee joints for the remaining pedal angles, checking the bend direction and leg lengths.

Still computing the knee joints for the remaining pedal angles, checking the bend direction and leg lengths.

Still working on the SVG, now the legs: I'm animating the leg path through precomputed knee positions and planning the crank and foot movement.

Working out the foot's path next: a circle of radius 28 centered on the wheel hub, traced clockwise on screen so the pedal passes through the bottom first, matching the crank's rotation direction.

Still writing the SVG's motion: the foot follows the pedal along the circle, and the legs use keyframed path shapes that stay in step with the crank.

Still working on the SVG: the wheel is set to scroll the ground markings left, and I'm planning a faint parallax for the hills and clouds. Next I'm sketching the anteater itself, with its long snout, grey-brown body, and striped chest, sitting upright on the seat.

I'm picturing the anteater's head tilted up so its snout points toward the bottles, but the hands and snout would crowd each other if the snout reaches out to the right. I'm weighing whether to have it face forward and watch the juggling from a different angle.

I'm weighing where the thrown bottles should start: if they launch from the right hand straight up near x=500, they'd cut across the snout, so I'm thinking the throws should begin nearer the center and arc outward so they clear the head.

I'm weighing whether the thrown bottles can cross in front of the snout without cluttering the picture. Pointing the snout steeper or shortening it doesn't clear the path, so I'm considering a side-view layout where both arms reach forward and the juggling happens in front of the animal.

Still picturing the anteater's pose: the hands would need to reach far out to the right to juggle clear of the snout, which would mean arms too long to be believable. I'm deciding to accept that the bottles will overlap the head, drawing them in front of it as a cartoon would.

I'm weighing whether the head should tilt up to watch the bottles or stay level, and I'm leaning toward a snout that droops down with a gentle curve since that's the classic silhouette. I'm also considering a slight head bob of about four degrees to follow the bottles. Then I'm thinking about raising the hands high, around y=150, so the arms sit above the snout instead of crossing it.

I'm trying the arms raised high, with hands near y=140 and the bottles arcing above the head. The right arm would cut across the snout, so I'm considering putting it behind the head or simply drawing the bottles in front of the snout.

Still working out the juggling pattern, which will be a three-bottle cascade tracing a figure-eight, with each throw starting inside and landing outside.

I'm working out how to animate the juggled bottles: x moves linearly while y needs an ease-out on the way up and an ease-in on the way down, so I'm looking at a cubic-bezier keySplines setting that reproduces that parabolic timing.

Working out the timing for the juggled bottles: the vertical motion needs an ease-out on the way up and an ease-in on the way down, which a cubic-bezier keySplines pair can reproduce exactly. To drive x and y independently, I'll nest the bottle in two groups so each axis gets its own animation.

Still writing the juggling animation: each bottle's horizontal and vertical motion will sit in nested groups so the two axes can be timed separately.

Still working out the ball timing: each ball gets a flight of about 0.8s and a hold of 0.4s, so the cycle runs 2.4s and the two hands alternate every 0.4s.

I'm laying out the bottle timing now: each ball is thrown from one hand to the other at a height of about 50 px, with a short hold in between, and the cycle repeats over 2.4 seconds.

Still writing the bottle timing: the x positions run through the flight and hold keyframes with linear motion, and I'm working out how the hands should move during the holds.

Still working out the bottle timing: the vertical motion alternates between ease-out on the way up and ease-in on the way down, with a small dip during each hold so the catch and throw feel continuous.

Still working out the bottle timing: the right hand throws at 0, 0.8 and 1.6 seconds while the left hand throws at 0.4, 1.2 and 2.0, so the throws alternate every 0.4 seconds.

Still working out the right hand's cycle: it moves empty from the inside position out to the far side over the first 0.4 seconds, then carries the bottle back in with the same dip as the ball.

Still writing the animation timing: the right hand's y-values follow a flat, dip, and rise pattern with the matching spline curves, and the left hand gets the mirror-image schedule.

Still writing the SVG's animation timing, now for the arms: they need to follow the hands, so I'm working out how the shoulder joints and elbows should move with them. The far-side legs and crank will use the same negative begin offset to stay in step with the bottles.

Still weighing how the arm should follow the hand: since the hand's x and y move on different easing curves, an arm drawn as a single quadratic path would drift slightly from the hand between keyframes, so I'm looking at whether the hand and arm can share one animation.

I'm considering making the hold motion of the ball piecewise linear in both x and y, so the arm's path keyframes can match it exactly without drift.

Still refining the bottle motion: I'm giving the hold section eased x-values so the arm's path animation can share the same spline timing as the ball and stay locked to it.

Working out the empty-hand return now: the right hand goes from the inside spot back out to the far side along a gentle arc, and I'm keeping it on a simple linear curve for that stretch.

Still writing the right hand's keyframes for the juggling cycle, and I'm settling on spline timing for the arm's path so it stays locked to the ball.

Still writing the arm paths: I'm working out the right arm's quadratic curve from the shoulder down to the hand at each keyframe, with the elbow drooping below the midpoint.

Still working out the arm paths: the right arm's control points follow the midpoint of each hand position, so the drooping elbow stays consistent through the cycle. I'm also reconsidering the juggling width, since the arms look stubby at this span.

Still working out the layout: I'm shifting the juggling pattern outward so the arms aren't too short, and I'm checking whether the catch point on the right would collide with the snout. I'll move the snout tip up and the hands down so the bottle clears it.

Still working out the head: I'm going to tilt the snout upward so it looks toward the bottles and clears the hands, keeping a slight downward curve so it still reads as an anteater. I'll draw the head in local coordinates pointing right and rotate the group by about -15°, with a small oscillation between -18° and -10° to follow the juggling.

Still writing the head shape: a long tapering path with a convex top, a rounded snout tip, and a bottom edge that curves back to the skull.

Still writing the head: I'm adding the eye, ear, nose, and mouth details, then a tongue that flicks out using a dash-offset animation.

Still writing the torso and head placement: I'm drawing a pear-shaped body from the seat up to the neck, then attaching the head so its back end sits at the top of the torso.

Settling the colors next: a grey-brown body, with the head a touch lighter.

Still writing the SVG colors: the body gets a grey-brown fill, the head a lighter tone, and the arms, legs, and tail each get their own shades.

Still writing the SVG: I'm drawing the tail as a big bushy plume that sweeps up and left from the rear, with a few fringe strokes, and giving it a slight sway.

I'm thinking about whether the whole upper body should sway a little for balance, rotating the torso, head, arms, and tail around the seat. If the bottles are grouped in with it, the pattern would sway as one piece, which might look natural, and since the hip stays near the pivot, the legs wouldn't be affected.

Still working out the upper body: I'm considering a slight sway of about 1.5° around the seat for the torso, head, arms, and bottles together, since the hips stay near the pivot and the legs wouldn't shift. I've decided against adding horizontal translation, since the ground scroll already implies steady motion.

Still writing the SVG: I'm placing the torso and seat so the seat peeks out just below the body, and I'm layering the far arm, torso, and near leg in front of the wheel.

Still writing the SVG: I'm laying out the legs and haunches, using darker tones for the hind legs and a dark thigh that overlaps the torso bottom.

Still working out the foot placement: the foot should sit above the pedal, so the ankle needs to be offset from the crank pin, and I'm weighing whether to shift the hip to keep the leg geometry consistent.

Still working out the wheel geometry: I'm moving the wheel centre down so the ankle circle sits clear of the pedals, giving a radius that puts the ground line around y = 546. From that I've got the circumference, which sets how far the ground marks should scroll per cycle.

Still writing the wheel: I'm laying out the crank and pedal positions around the hub, with the far crank hidden behind the tire, then drawing the tire, rim, and spokes.

Still writing the wheel details: I'm adding a reflector to a spoke so the rotation reads clearly, then drawing the fork and seat post from the hub up to the seat.

Still writing the ground: I'm building a green strip with a pattern of dashes and pebbles, sized to repeat every 103.67 px so it can scroll smoothly with the wheel.

Still writing the background: I'm building the hills as a path with a period of 800px, so they can drift slowly across the scene, and I'm adding clouds that loop left over time.

Still writing the hills: I'm checking that the curve joins cleanly at the 800px repeat point, and I'm adjusting the control point so the slope matches on both sides.

Still writing the SVG: I'm drawing the bottle shapes now, a rounded body with a narrowing neck and a cap, sized to juggle along the arcs.

Still writing the bottle shapes: I'm adding the neck, cap, and label details, then rotating each one to spin once per throw.

Still working out the bottle spin: I'm setting the rotation so each one flips a full turn during its flight and holds steady by the neck in each hand.

Still working out the bottle spin: each one turns a full revolution during its flight and settles upright in the hand, with a slight tilt in the right hand so it reads as a paw holding it.

Still working out the bottle spin: I'm setting the keyframes so each one turns about 375° during its flight and settles upright in the hand, with a slight tilt in each paw. Next I'm adding the paws as small light circles with dark claws, layered in front of the bottles.

Still writing the arm and paw animation: I'm checking whether the claws can ride along with the arm endpoint using the same keyframes, so the grip stays in step with the bottles.

Still working out the arm keyframes: the right arm starts at the shoulder and dips into a gentle droop toward the first hand position, and I'm checking where the elbow control point should sit for each of the four hand positions.

Still writing the left arm: I'm working out its keyframes by mirroring the right arm's path about the centre line, with the same droop pattern.

Still writing the left arm's keyframes: I'm mirroring the right arm's control points across the centre line so the shoulder sits at x = 372 and the droop matches on both sides.

Still writing the keyframes: I'm finishing the left arm's path values and spline timing, then setting the right arm's splines to match, before moving on to the ball's horizontal positions.

Still writing the animation: I'm checking that each ball's horizontal and vertical keyframes line up with the hand positions, so a ball in the left hand during the hold phase matches the paw's dip.

Checking the ball timing against the hand positions: the ball thrown from the right hand lands in the left hand at 0.8s, and the phase offsets for the other two balls line up with the holds. I'm keeping the keyTimes at 0.33333 rather than 0.3333 so the spline progress stays matched across the animations.

Still working out the head's position: I'm checking where the snout tip lands once the head is tilted up, so the bottle arc clears it.

Still working out the snout's position: after tilting the head up, the tip lands around (547, 163), which sits above the right hand's catch point at (530, 255), so the descending bottles should pass just in front of it.

Still writing the torso: I'm shaping the body path with a slight forward lean and a gently rounded bottom, then adding a dark throat stripe clipped to it with a lighter border.

Still writing the tail: I'm checking whether its upper edge clears the left hand's catch point at (270,255), since the plume's curve passes close to that area.

Still working out the tail: I'm lowering its upper edge so it sweeps more horizontally toward the left, so it stays clear of the left hand's catch point.

Still writing the tail: I'm lowering its upper edge into a drooping leaf shape that sweeps left and clears the hands, then closing the lower edge back to the base.

Still writing the tail's sway and the upper body: I'm adding a slight wobble to the whole upper group about the hip, and I'm ordering the layers so the far leg and wheel sit behind the torso.

Still writing the upper body: I'm adding a rounded haunch behind the leg at the hip, so the thigh reads as part of the body.

Still writing the leg: I'm adding a darker ellipse at the hip as a haunch, then computing the near leg's path points at each crank angle so the knee and ankle follow the pedal.

Still working out the leg keyframes: I'm computing the near knee and ankle positions at each crank angle, using straight segments so the thigh reads as a bent leg, and I'm accepting the small chord error since the foot covers it.

Still working out the wheel's rotation: I'm setting the circular path for the crank so the foot starts at the bottom and travels clockwise on screen, which moves the ground left as the wheel turns.

Still writing the SVG scene: I'm placing the wheel's shadow under the ground line and layering in drifting clouds that loop behind the bottles.

Still writing the ground pattern: I'm tiling pebbles and tufts across the road band and aligning the pattern's origin so the tile boundaries line up with the rect's top edge. Next I'm starting the head.

Still writing the head: I'm adding the ear, a bit of cheek shading, and the nose and mouth, then a tongue whose dash offset animates so it flicks in and out.

Still writing the tongue: I'm drawing it behind the head so it stays hidden at the start, using butt caps to avoid a stray dot at the tip.

Still writing the arm and paw details: the tongue's dash timing is in place, and now I'm giving the forelegs a light grey stroke with a dark paw and small claws, with the bottles layered in front.

Still writing the foot details: I'm filling in the ellipse and claws, then wrapping it in a group so the animation can run on it.

Still writing the tail: I'm adding the claw strokes, a streaked texture along the tail, and the tail's outline path.

Still writing the SVG's leg paths: I'm setting the near and far leg keyframes so the knee and foot positions follow the pedal crank.

arguments.content:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 600" width="800" height="600" role="img" aria-labelledby="title">
  <title id="title">An anteater riding a unicycle while juggling bottles</title>

  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="sky" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#8fd3f4"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#eef9ff"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="headGrad" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#85776b"/>
      <stop offset="0.3" stop-color="#85776b"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#c6baab"/>
    </linearGradient>

    <!-- one tile = 1/4 wheel circumference, so the ground scroll matches the wheel -->
    <pattern id="dirt" x="0" y="546" width="103.67" height="54" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
      <ellipse cx="20" cy="14" rx="9" ry="2.5" fill="#b9975c"/>
      <ellipse cx="70" cy="32" rx="12" ry="3" fill="#b9975c"/>
      <circle cx="46" cy="44" r="2.5" fill="#9c7a48"/>
      <ellipse cx="92" cy="11" rx="4" ry="1.5" fill="#9c7a48"/>
      <circle cx="8" cy="36" r="1.8" fill="#9c7a48"/>
    </pattern>

    <clipPath id="torsoClip">
      <path d="M362,338 C338,310 340,225 378,192 C400,174 438,180 446,212 C456,262 448,312 428,338 C410,346 380,346 362,338 Z"/>
    </clipPath>

    <g id="cloud" fill="#fff" fill-opacity="0.9">
      <ellipse cx="0" cy="0" rx="48" ry="17"/>
      <ellipse cx="-20" cy="-12" rx="22" ry="16"/>
      <ellipse cx="12" cy="-17" rx="28" ry="20"/>
    </g>

    <!-- bottle, centred on its origin; glass colour is inherited from <use fill> -->
    <g id="bottle">
      <rect x="-5" y="-35" width="10" height="6" rx="1.5" fill="#e3c04a"/>

      <circle cx="0" cy="13" r="3.5" fill="#d9534f"/>
      <path d="M-6,-1 V3 M-6,23 V27" stroke="#fff" stroke-opacity="0.55" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>
    </g>

    <!-- foot + pedal, origin at the ankle; foot colour inherited -->
    <g id="foot">
      <rect x="-15" y="7" width="30" height="6" rx="2" fill="#333"/>
      <ellipse cx="5" cy="1" rx="17" ry="8"/>
      <path d="M20,0 l6,3 M19,4 l5,4" stroke="#2b2522" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"/>
    </g>

    <!-- paw, origin at the wrist -->
    <g id="paw">
      <circle r="13" fill="#3b322d"/>
      <path d="M-8,-9 q-4,-9 2,-13 M0,-12 q-2,-9 5,-12 M8,-9 q0,-9 8,-10" stroke="#2b2522" stroke-width="3.5" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/>

  <circle cx="675" cy="95" r="42" fill="#ffe27a"/>

    <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" from="0 0" to="-900 0" dur="70s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    <use href="#cloud" x="120" y="120"/>
    <use href="#cloud" transform="translate(440,75) scale(1.3)"/>
    <use href="#cloud" transform="translate(740,150) scale(0.8)"/>
    <use href="#cloud" x="1020" y="120"/>
    <use href="#cloud" transform="translate(1340,75) scale(1.3)"/>
    <use href="#cloud" transform="translate(1640,150) scale(0.8)"/>
  </g>

  <!-- rolling hills (800px period) -->
  <g>
    <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" from="0 0" to="-800 0" dur="40s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    <path fill="#8cc474" d="M0,460 C100,400 200,400 300,450 C380,490 450,420 560,430 C680,440 750,490 800,460 C900,400 1000,400 1100,450 C1180,490 1250,420 1360,430 C1480,440 1550,490 1600,460 L1600,560 L0,560 Z"/>
  </g>
  <g>
    <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" from="0 0" to="-800 0" dur="16s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    <path fill="#74b25c" d="M0,520 C120,490 220,500 330,515 C440,530 520,495 640,500 C720,503 760,530 800,520 C920,490 1020,500 1130,515 C1240,530 1320,495 1440,500 C1520,503 1560,530 1600,520 L1600,560 L0,560 Z"/>

  <!-- ground -->

    <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" from="0 0" to="-103.67 0" dur="0.5s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
  </rect>
  <rect x="0" y="546" width="800" height="4" fill="#b08d55"/>
  <ellipse cx="400" cy="553" rx="62" ry="6" fill="#000" fill-opacity="0.2"/>

  <!-- ===== Far side: crank, leg, foot ===== -->
  <g>
    <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate" from="180 400 480" to="540 400 480" dur="2s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    <line x1="400" y1="480" x2="428" y2="480" stroke="#444" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/>
  </g>
  <path fill="none" stroke="#4a3e37" stroke-width="22" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M392,335 L437,410.6 L372,470">
    <animate attributeName="d" dur="2s" begin="-1s" repeatCount="indefinite"
      values="M392,335 L461.7,388.7 L428,470;
              M392,335 L444.8,405.4 L419.8,489.8;
              M392,335 L428.9,414.9 L400,498;
              M392,335 L427.4,415.6 L380.2,489.8;
              M392,335 L437,410.6 L372,470;
              M392,335 L452,399.4 L380.2,450.2;
              M392,335 L465.6,383.3 L400,442;
              M392,335 L469.2,377.3 L419.8,450.2;
              M392,335 L461.7,388.7 L428,470"/>

content.text:
I wrote the animated SVG to `anteater-unicycle.svg` in the working directory; I haven't rendered it here, so open it in a browser to check how it looks.

What the animation contains:

- **Anteater**: it faces right, with a long snout, a flicking tongue, a blinking eye, the black-and-white shoulder stripe and a swaying bushy tail. Its upper body wobbles slightly for balance.
- **Unicycle**: the wheel, cranks and pedals turn together, and both legs pedal with knees that bend to follow the pedals. The ground scrolls at the wheel's rolling speed, with hills and clouds drifting behind.
- **Juggling**: three bottles (green, amber, blue) fly in a cascade pattern, flipping once per throw. The paws move to catch, scoop and throw each bottle in time.

The bottles pass in front of the anteater's head on their way up, since the juggling is drawn flat in front of the body.

It uses SVG's built-in animation only (no JavaScript or CSS).
